nodes.rationale: Behavioral economics is a well-established subfield of economics studying the effects of psychological, cognitive, and emotional factors on economic decisions; it has its own journals, conferences, Nobel laureates (Kahneman 2002, Thaler 2017), and university course offerings, meeting the discipline-node bar as a subfield of field:economics.

nodes.source_hint: Order-supplied Wikidata hint Q1971461 for 'social choice theory'; cross-check against Wikipedia 'Social choice theory' and standard economics/political-science discipline classifications.
nodes.rationale: Social choice theory is an established theoretical framework studying collective decision-making, voting, and welfare aggregation (Arrow's impossibility theorem, Sen's work); it has a dedicated academic society (Society for Social Choice and Welfare), a dedicated journal, and is standardly taught as a distinct subfield within economics (with strong ties to political science and philosophy).
nodes.uncertainty: The order-supplied QID Q1971461 is an unverified hint — QC must live-verify referent and P31/P279 typing. Boundary question: social choice theory sits at the economics/political-science/philosophy intersection; this proposal anchors it under field:economics per the order, but QC should consider whether a §13 cross-listing to political science is warranted (deferred here, not resolved).

nodes.rationale: Thaler is one of the principal founders of behavioral economics, integrating psychological realism into economic theory across a body of work from the late 1970s onward (mental accounting, endowment effect, nudge theory with Cass Sunstein); he received the 2017 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences explicitly for this founding contribution.
nodes.uncertainty: QID Q92610 is an untrusted training-recall hint (born 1945) — QC must live-verify P31=Q5, P569 present, and P570 absent (aliveness is an observed fact for QC to confirm, not an assertion made here). LIVING PERSON — living-person handling v2 applies (decision (70)): stricter evidence floor (resolver-verified identity + ≥2 independent live claim-stating sources + conservative wording), auto-promotes when clean and no escalation signal fires. Co-founding is plural: Kahneman and Tversky's heuristics-and-biases program predates and underlies Thaler's behavioral-economics program (record-not-resolve — see the paired Kahneman edge below); some framings credit Kahneman/Tversky as the foundational psychological input and Thaler as the economist who built the subfield institutionally (Journal of Behavioral Economics, NBER working group). QID may be wrong.

nodes.rationale: Sen made foundational contributions to social choice theory (his 1970 book 'Collective Choice and Social Welfare' extended and reformulated Arrow's framework, introducing new axiomatic approaches and the liberal paradox) and is a central, widely-cited figure whose work substantially shaped the modern field; he received the 1998 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for contributions to welfare economics, including social choice theory.
nodes.uncertainty: QID Q125106 is an untrusted training-recall hint (born 1933) — QC must live-verify P31=Q5, P569 present, P570 absent. REFERENT-PRECISION FLAG (the order names this explicitly): Sen's Nobel citation and broader legacy are often framed as 'welfare economics' rather than 'social choice theory' narrowly, and Kenneth Arrow (not in this batch) is the more standard 'founder' of modern social choice theory (Arrow's Impossibility Theorem, 1951, predates Sen's 1970 book by two decades) — Sen is more accurately a central/formalizing figure than the originating founder. QC should weigh whether `founded_or_formalized` (vs. a weaker relation, or targeting subfield:welfare-economics instead — which does not yet exist in the corpus) is the correct claim, and whether Arrow should be added as a companion node before this edge is promoted.

nodes.rationale: Langacker is a principal founder of cognitive linguistics, developing Cognitive Grammar (starting with his 1976 UC San Diego work and the two-volume 'Foundations of Cognitive Grammar', 1987/1991) as one of the field's foundational theoretical frameworks, alongside George Lakoff's cognitive semantics program.

nodes.rationale: Mandelbrot coined the term 'fractal' in 1975 ('Les objets fractals: forme, hasard et dimension') and, through 'The Fractal Geometry of Nature' (1982), founded fractal geometry as a coherent mathematical field describing self-similar and non-integer-dimensional structures; he is universally credited as the founder of fractal geometry. Mandelbrot died in 2010.
